proposals.explanation: Ambire offers in-app fiat-to-crypto buying via integrated providers (Ramp Network, Transak, MoonPay, Guardarian) from the wallet's Deposit tab.
Ambire released an in-app fiat off-ramp (via Guardarian and MoonPay) letting users sell crypto and receive cash directly to their bank account.
The MoonPay integration supports credit/debit cards (Visa, Mastercard) for buying crypto in-app, and Transak supports card purchases too.
The MoonPay integration in Ambire explicitly supports Apple Pay as a payment method for buying crypto.
The MoonPay integration in Ambire explicitly supports Google Pay as a payment method for buying crypto.
Ambire's ramps support bank transfer methods (SEPA, ACH, wire) via MoonPay and Guardarian for both on- and off-ramping.
Ready lets users buy crypto via Ramp or Banxa using Apple Pay, per its funding tutorial and Card FAQs.
Ready's integrated Ramp/Banxa on-ramp supports Google Pay as a payment method for buying crypto.
Ready supports bank transfer for buying/funding crypto via Banxa/Ramp (also virtual bank details for USDC deposits).
Ready displays accumulated/claimable staking rewards and lets users claim them directly in the app.
Base App buys crypto via integrated Coinbase Onramp, which supports debit card payments (guest checkout with debit card is explicitly available).
Base App announced buying crypto with Apple Pay, and Coinbase Onramp (its integrated ramp) lists Apple Pay as a supported payment method.
Coinbase Onramp, the ramp integrated into Base App, lists Google Pay as a supported payment method.
Coinbase Onramp supports funding from a linked bank account (ACH), available in-app when a Coinbase account is connected.

Base App/Coinbase Wallet aggregates multiple wallets by connecting self-custodial wallets via WalletConnect (wallets the user controls), with no documented ability to add public addresses you do not hold keys for as watch-only.
Ramp Network (Brave Wallet's integrated on/off-ramp) supports Visa/Mastercard debit and credit cards per Ramp's official payment-methods support page.
Ramp supports Apple Pay (with a linked Visa/Mastercard), as confirmed by Ramp's payment-methods page and Brave's own off-ramp blog stating Ramp integrates Apple Pay.
Ramp supports Google Pay (with a linked Visa/Mastercard) per Ramp's official payment-methods page, and Brave's off-ramp blog lists Google Pay among Ramp's integrated methods.

Ramp supports bank transfers (SEPA/Easy Bank Transfer/manual transfers) per its payment-methods page, and Brave's off-ramp blog confirms bank transfers are among Ramp's supported methods in Brave Wallet.

Brave Wallet's official import options cover only recovery phrase, private key, and JSON keystore imports, with no documented ability to add a public address as a watch-only/view-only account; the internal 'Watch-Only' NFT label merely flags unowned NFTs rather than a deliberate watch-address feature.
Coinbase Wallet's official 'Sell or cash out crypto' help article confirms an in-app crypto-to-fiat off-ramp (cash out) available in 130+ countries via a Coinbase account or third-party providers.

Coinbase states transactions on Coinbase Wallet are not included in cost-basis/gain-loss calculations (assumed $0 cost basis), and no source shows the wallet tracking acquisition cost basis of holdings.

The Daimo consumer app integrated Coinbase Onramp for in-app deposits/buying (on-ramp) only; its withdrawal was on-chain crypto withdrawal, and neither the archived app README (github.com/daimo-eth/daimo) nor Daimo docs document any in-app crypto-to-fiat sell/off-ramp.
Coinbase Onramp was live in the Daimo app as its in-app buy/deposit provider, and Coinbase Onramp's supported payment methods include debit cards per Coinbase's developer documentation.
Elytro's official site and FAQ describe only on-chain features (send/receive, swap, bridge, stablecoin gas) with no fiat-to-crypto on-ramp mentioned anywhere.
No crypto-to-fiat off-ramp is mentioned on Elytro's site or FAQ; the wallet only supports on-chain swaps/bridges, not cashing out to fiat.
Since Elytro has no integrated fiat ramp, no card payment method is available; the official site lists only on-chain operations.
No fiat ramp exists in Elytro, so Apple Pay is not offered as a payment method per the official site and FAQ.
No fiat ramp exists in Elytro, so Google Pay is not offered as a payment method per the official site and FAQ.
No fiat ramp exists in Elytro, so bank transfer (ACH/SEPA/wire) is not available as a payment method per the official site and FAQ.
Family's fiat integration via Stripe is documented only for buying crypto (on-ramp); no sell/cash-out to fiat feature appears in Family's support or FAQ pages.

Frame is a desktop Ethereum dapp wallet with no integrated fiat on-ramp; its docs describe only hardware/software signers and watch accounts, and reviews confirm purchases must be done via external exchanges.
Frame provides no in-app crypto-to-fiat off-ramp; there is no buy/sell functionality in the wallet, only dapp connectivity and signing.
With no fiat ramp present in Frame, there is no card payment method available.
With no fiat ramp present in Frame, Apple Pay is not available.
With no fiat ramp present in Frame, Google Pay is not available.
With no fiat ramp present in Frame, bank transfer is not available.
Frame's docs describe Watch Accounts that are 'solely for viewing assets and connecting to protocols' without signing, i.e. watch-only accounts.
Gem Wallet's fiat provider docs list integrated on-ramp providers (Mercuryo, MoonPay, Transak, Paybis, Banxa, Cash App) that let users buy crypto in-app.
The docs state Mercuryo, MoonPay, Transak and Paybis support both buying and selling crypto (fiat off-ramp) within Gem Wallet.
The fiat provider docs state users can buy crypto with traditional payment methods such as cards.
The fiat provider docs state buying is available via 'supported bank payment options' alongside cards and mobile payments.
Guides describing Gem Wallet cover balances and staking but no profit/loss tracking, and reviews note portfolio-tracking limitations.
No source indicates Gem Wallet tracks acquisition cost basis; it displays current balances only.
Gem Wallet offers its own native staking but reviews note it is missing DeFi positions, meaning it does not surface external DeFi protocol positions.
imToken integrates MoonPay (and OpenC) for in-app fiat-to-crypto purchases via a 'Buy' button on the wallet home, per imToken's help center and the MoonPay partnership announcement.
imToken's help documentation states the MoonPay integration lets users pay with Visa (card), alongside Apple Pay and Google Pay.
imToken's help documentation states the MoonPay integration supports Apple Pay as a payment method for buying tokens.
imToken's help documentation states the MoonPay integration supports Google Pay as a payment method for buying tokens.
The DeBank-powered DeFi Portfolio Manager surfaces lending/borrowing positions (loans) across protocols like Aave and Compound.
The DeBank-powered DeFi Portfolio Manager surfaces AMM/DEX liquidity-pool balances (e.g. Uniswap, PancakeSwap positions).
The DeBank-powered DeFi Portfolio Manager surfaces yield-vault/yield-aggregator and farm positions among the DeFi balances it displays.
Mt Pelerin's official buy-crypto page confirms Bridge Wallet's integrated buy feature supports Apple Pay for instant crypto purchases.
NuFi's official support page states you can buy crypto via the integrated MoonPay ramp using 'a bank card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, bank transfer and other payment options.'
NuFi's official 'How to buy crypto' support page explicitly lists Apple Pay as a supported payment method through the integrated MoonPay ramp.
NuFi's official 'How to buy crypto' support page explicitly lists Google Pay as a supported payment method through the integrated MoonPay ramp.
NuFi's official 'How to buy crypto' support page explicitly lists bank transfer as a supported payment method through the integrated MoonPay ramp.

NuFi's 'Add Account' options are limited to creating hot wallet accounts tied to your own seed phrase or pairing hardware wallets you hold keys for, with no option to add a watch-only/view-only address.
Phantom's official help center documents an in-app crypto-to-fiat off-ramp via a 'Sell Crypto' flow (Home > Cash > Add Cash > Sell Crypto) and a 'Withdraw crypto to your bank account' feature.
Phantom's help center confirms bank transfer as a supported method for funding/withdrawing the Cash account, including a dedicated 1:1 USD bank withdrawal to your own bank account.

Phantom lets users access lending dApps (e.g. Kamino, Aave) via its dApp browser but its own portfolio/Terminal only surfaces token balances and its native trading/perps positions, not external lending/borrowing positions, which require third-party trackers like Step Finance.
No official or reputable source indicates Phantom surfaces liquidity-pool positions held in external protocols; its portfolio shows balances and native trading positions only.
No evidence Phantom reads/displays external yield-vault positions; its native views cover token balances and Phantom's own products rather than aggregating third-party vault positions.
Liquidation levels/warnings in Phantom's Terminal apply only to its own Hyperliquid-powered perps product, not to borrow positions in external DeFi lending protocols.

The current PillarX App Store listing's release notes (v3.31.1, 09/02/2025) state the app "removed the option to buy and sell using third party sites," and the current description only lists cross-chain swaps and stablecoin gas with no fiat on-ramp.
The same App Store release notes (v3.31.1, 09/02/2025) confirm buy AND sell via third-party providers was removed, so the current shipping PillarX app offers no fiat off-ramp.
With in-app buy/sell removed in the current PillarX app (v3.31.1, 09/02/2025), no fiat ramp exists, so card payments are not available in the shipping product.
No in-app fiat ramp exists in the current PillarX app after buy/sell was removed (v3.31.1, 09/02/2025), so Apple Pay is not offered as a ramp payment method.
No in-app fiat ramp exists in the current PillarX app after buy/sell was removed (v3.31.1, 09/02/2025), so Google Pay is not offered as a ramp payment method.
No in-app fiat ramp exists in the current PillarX app after buy/sell was removed (v3.31.1, 09/02/2025), so bank transfer is not offered as a ramp payment method.
Multiple reviews confirm Rabby has no fiat on-ramp; the CryptoSlate review states 'There is also no fiat on-ramp of any kind,' with users funding via external transfers only.
Rabby has no fiat ramps at all, so no crypto-to-fiat off-ramp exists in-app.
With no fiat on-ramp present in Rabby, no card payment method is offered.
No fiat ramp exists in Rabby, so Apple Pay is not available as a payment method.
No fiat ramp exists in Rabby, so Google Pay is not available as a payment method.
No fiat ramp exists in Rabby, so bank transfer is not available as a payment method.
Rainbow's official support page states it does not support selling crypto to fiat within the app and instead directs users to transfer assets to a centralized exchange to cash out.
Rainbow's buy-crypto guide lists Apple Pay as a supported payment method across its integrated on-ramp providers (Ramp, MoonPay, Coinbase Pay).
Rainbow's buy-crypto guide lists ACH (bank transfers) as a supported payment method via its on-ramp providers.
Rainbow's DeFi positions page lists only Aave, Compound, Yearn, and Maker, none of which are liquidity-pool protocols (no Uniswap, Curve, or Balancer), so LP positions are not surfaced.
Safe{Wallet}'s only documented fiat ramp is a MoonPay-powered buy/on-ramp for iOS; no official source describes an off-ramp or selling crypto to fiat.
Safe's official on-ramp announcement states users can buy crypto within Safe{Wallet} using debit/credit card or Apple Pay via MoonPay.
Trust Wallet offers an in-app crypto-to-fiat off-ramp via integrated providers like MoonPay and Ramp, with a Sell button that connects users to convert crypto to fiat.
Trust Wallet's official announcement states it supports Apple Pay as a buy-crypto payment option via its Express Buy feature powered by third-party partners.
Trust Wallet's official announcement states it supports Google Pay as a buy-crypto payment option via its Express Buy feature powered by third-party partners.
Uniswap's integrated fiat on-ramp accepts bank cards including MasterCard, Visa and Maestro (debit/credit) as a payment method.
Uniswap's ramp supports Apple Pay, listed among accepted payment methods and available via integrated providers such as Revolut, MoonPay and Transak.
The official Uniswap blog confirms the Revolut on-ramp in Uniswap supports Google Pay ("Revolut Pay, Apple Pay, Google Pay, cards").
Uniswap's fiat on-ramp supports bank transfers (including SEPA and US/UK/Brazil bank transfers) as a payment method.
The Uniswap app surfaces liquidity positions with uncollected/claimable fees that users can collect directly in the UI via the Collect fees action.
Zerion's own help center states "Currently, Zerion doesn't support selling crypto directly for fiat currencies" and requires transferring to an external exchange to cash out.
Zerion's funding guide lists integrated providers MoonPay and Mercuryo as supporting Apple Pay as a payment method for buying crypto.
Zerion's funding guide lists MoonPay (integrated provider) as supporting Google Pay as a payment method for buying crypto in-app.
Zerion's funding guide states its integrated ramps (MoonPay, Ramp, Mercuryo) support bank transfers including SEPA/SEPA Instant and Faster Payments Service.
Zerion's Profit and Loss feature tracks "Average Cost" (cost basis of holdings) and invested amount per asset to compute realized/unrealized gains.

Zeus is a self-custodial desktop Ethereum wallet whose README lists its features (send, bridge, swap, portfolio, simulations) with no fiat on-ramp, and explicitly states it does not rely on any third-party service.
The README documents no crypto-to-fiat off-ramp; only crypto operations like swaps and bridging are supported, and a GitHub code search found zero references to any ramp providers.
Zeus has no fiat ramp at all, so card payments are not available as a purchase method.
Zeus has no fiat ramp, so Apple Pay is not available as a payment method.
Zeus has no fiat ramp, so Google Pay is not available as a payment method.
Zeus has no fiat ramp, so bank transfer (ACH/SEPA/wire) is not available as a payment method.
